LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: IMAGINATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing (2 sessions) • Forming simple para
Topic 3.5: Guided Writing: Imaginative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Imaginative Writing, part of Writing 3.3 Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing (2 sessions) • Forming simple para in Grade 7 ARABIC.

Key inquiry question: How can you develop a creative text?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to research the features of imaginative writing from print and non-print sources,

2. collaborate with peers to organise ideas on the theme using mind maps,

3. write an imaginative composition on the theme using the organised ideas,

4. share their compositions with peers for review,

5. publish the best compositions in the school or public magazine.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to research the features of imaginative writing from print and non-print sources,
2. collaborate with peers to organise ideas on the theme using mind maps,
3. write an imaginative composition on the theme using the organised ideas,
4. share their compositions with peers for review,
5. publish the best compositions in the school or public magazine.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Imaginative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: Research skills are developed as the learner collaborates with peers to explore

information on features of imaginative compositions from print and non-print sources.

• Self-efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner embraces public expression skills when publishing the best compositions in

the school or public magazine.

45

Values:
Love: This is promoted as the learner exhibits a caring attitude when giving constructive feedback to peers on their work

during the peer review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-management (Time management): This is promoted as the learner establishes ways of using their time constructively for

fun and enjoyment and using this information when writing the compositions.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of imaginative compositions to their learning of creative writing texts in English.
